claim: Dysregulated cytokine expression by T cells plays a pivotal role in the pathogenesis of autoimmune diseases.
source: Dysregulated cytokine expression by T cells plays a pivotal role in the pathogenesis of autoimmune diseases.
evidence: This is a general statement about the role of T cells in autoimmune diseases, drawing from established scientific understanding.

claim: A super-functional follicular helper T cell (Tfh)-like subpopulation was identified in lupus-prone NZBxW mice using the PRI approach.
source: Here, we were able to identify a super-functional follicular helper T cell (Tfh)-like subpopulation in lupus-prone NZBxW mice with our binning approach "pattern recognition of immune cells (PRI)".
evidence: The manuscript describes the identification of this subpopulation using their novel PRI method, supported by experimental data throughout the results section.

claim: The identified super-functional T cell subpopulation is characterized as IL-21+ IFN-γhigh PD-1low CD40Lhigh CXCR5- Bcl-6-.
source: PRI uncovered a subpopulation of IL-21+ IFN-γhigh PD-1low CD40Lhigh CXCR5- Bcl-6- T cells specifically expanded in diseased mice.
evidence: This characterization is based on flow cytometry data presented in multiple figures throughout the manuscript.

claim: The super-functional T cells express high levels of TNF-α and IL-2.
source: In addition, these cells express high levels of TNF-α and IL-2, and provide B cell help for IgG production in an IL-21 and CD40L dependent manner.
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in figures analyzing cytokine expression patterns.

claim: The super-functional T cells provide B cell help for IgG production in an IL-21 and CD40L dependent manner.
source: In addition, these cells express high levels of TNF-α and IL-2, and provide B cell help for IgG production in an IL-21 and CD40L dependent manner.
evidence: This is demonstrated by co-culture experiments with blocking antibodies shown in Figure 7.

claim: CD4 T cells play a major role in autoimmune diseases such as systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) by accumulating as autoreactive disease-promoting memory cells and amplifying inflammation as well as providing B cell help.
source: CD4 T cells play a major role in autoimmune diseases such as systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) by accumulating as autoreactive disease-promoting memory cells and amplifying inflammation as well as providing B cell help (Suárez-Fueyo et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Dysregulated cytokine production, metabolic alterations and aberrant cell signalling cause abnormalities in T cell differentiation and hyperactivation of B cells and thus contribute to lupus disease.
source: It is known that dysregulated cytokine production, metabolic alterations and aberrant cell signalling cause abnormalities in T cell differentiation and hyperactivation of B cells and thus contribute to lupus disease (Moulton et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Progressive SLE disease is associated with lower expression of TNF-α, IFN-γ, and IL-2.
source: For SLE, there are several studies in mouse models and humans, showing that the progressive disease is associated with lower expression of TNF-α, IFN-γ, and IL-2 (Humrich et al., 2010) as well as higher expression of PD-1 (Jiao et al., 2014), IL-21 (Wang et al., 2014), and IL-10 (Facciotti et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Progressive SLE disease is associated with higher expression of PD-1.
source: For SLE, there are several studies in mouse models and humans, showing that the progressive disease is associated with lower expression of TNF-α, IFN-γ, and IL-2 (Humrich et al., 2010) as well as higher expression of PD-1 (Jiao et al., 2014), IL-21 (Wang et al., 2014), and IL-10 (Facciotti et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Progressive SLE disease is associated with higher expression of IL-21.
source: For SLE, there are several studies in mouse models and humans, showing that the progressive disease is associated with lower expression of TNF-α, IFN-γ, and IL-2 (Humrich et al., 2010) as well as higher expression of PD-1 (Jiao et al., 2014), IL-21 (Wang et al., 2014), and IL-10 (Facciotti et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Progressive SLE disease is associated with higher expression of IL-10.
source: For SLE, there are several studies in mouse models and humans, showing that the progressive disease is associated with lower expression of TNF-α, IFN-γ, and IL-2 (Humrich et al., 2010) as well as higher expression of PD-1 (Jiao et al., 2014), IL-21 (Wang et al., 2014), and IL-10 (Facciotti et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: A comprehensive combinatorial characterization of T-cell subsets in SLE is still lacking.
source: Despite the detection of these individual parameters, a comprehensive combinatorial characterization of T-cell subsets in SLE is still lacking.
evidence: This is an assessment of the current state of the field based on the authors' review of the literature.

claim: Recent articles have revealed enormous and unexpected heterogeneity and complexity in T cell subpopulations with partially overlapping properties and functions.
source: Recent articles have revealed enormous and unexpected heterogeneity and complexity in T cell subpopulations with partially overlapping properties and functions of the cell subsets, such as follicular T helper (Tfh) and Tfh-like cell subsets (Trüb et al., 2017; Wong et al., 2015; Wong et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to recent literature.

claim: Human T peripheral helper cells (Tph) expand in autoimmune diseases.
source: Of particular interest are the recently observed human T peripheral helper cells (Tph), which expand in autoimmune diseases (Bocharnikov et al., 2019; Christophersen et al., 2019; Ekman et al., 2019; Rao et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to recent literature.

claim: Current analysis strategies based on clustering tend to find mainly cell-population clusters which are significantly high in phenotypical contrast.
source: Most of the current analysis strategies are based on clustering and the respective frequencies of the clusters (Levine et al., 2015; Qiu et al., 2011; Spitzer et al., 2015; Wong et al., 2016). The main problem with these methods is that they tend to find mainly cell-populationclusters which are significantly high in phenotypical contrast.
evidence: This is an assessment of clustering methods based on citations and the authors' understanding of their limitations.

claim: Cluster approaches are not very meaningful when cell subpopulations are very similar or even partially overlapping.
source: If the cell subpopulations are very similar or even partially overlapping, as in the present investigation, then a cluster approach is usually not very meaningful (Newell and Cheng, 2016; O'Neill et al., 2013; Saeys et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to literature discussing limitations of clustering approaches.

claim: IFN-γ is almost exclusively produced by CD44+ cells in NZBxW mice.
source: As expected, IFN-γ is almost exclusively produced by CD44+ cells (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is demonstrated by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: The bins with the highest expression levels of IFN-γ are TNF-αhi CD44+ and are in an area with low cell density and low-to-intermediate frequency of IFN-γ.
source: Apparently, our bin plot comparison shows that the bins with the highest expression levels of IFN-γ are TNF-αhi CD44+ (Figure 1F) and are in an area with low cell density and low-to-intermediate frequency of IFN-γ (Figure 1E).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the bin plot analysis shown in Figures 1E and 1F.

claim: The IFN-γhighest bin area contains cells that are also high in IL-2, but low in PD-1.
source: This visualized that the IFN-γhighest bin area contains cells that are also high in IL-2, but low in PD-1 (Figure 1F).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the pseudo-multi-parametric viewing shown in Figure 1F.

claim: Increased frequencies of PD-1+ and IL-10+ cells are age- and disease-dependent in NZBxW mice.
source: Increased frequencies of PD-1+ and IL-10+ cells as well as decreased frequencies of IL-2+ and TNF-α+ cells were age- and disease-dependent (Figure 2A–C).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the disease kinetics data shown in Figure 2.

claim: Decreased frequencies of IL-2+ and TNF-α+ cells are age- and disease-dependent in NZBxW mice.
source: Increased frequencies of PD-1+ and IL-10+ cells as well as decreased frequencies of IL-2+ and TNF-α+ cells were age- and disease-dependent (Figure 2A–C).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the disease kinetics data shown in Figure 2.

claim: The co-production of cytokines changed in the course of the disease to a lower degree of poly-functionality, visible by the accumulation of non-producing and IFN-γ single-producing cells.
source: The co-production of the cytokines changed in the course of the disease to a lower degree of poly-functionality, visible by the accumulation of non-producing and IFN-γ single-producing cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Loss of poly-functionality is considered as a hallmark of chronic infections and often used as an end-point to evaluate exhaustion of CD8+ and CD4+ T cells.
source: As loss of poly-functionality is considered as a hallmark of chronic infections and often used as an end-point to evaluate exhaustion of CD8+ and CD4+ T cells (Larsen et al., 2012; Tilstra et al., 2018), we investigated the combinatorial expression of the four cytokines with PD-1.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: During disease progression of lupus nephritis, a higher expression of inhibitory receptor PD-1 was associated with a lower degree of CD4+ Tmem-cell functionality regarding IL-2, TNF-α and IFN-γ expression.
source: During disease progression of lupus nephritis, a higher expression of inhibitory receptor PD-1 was associated with a lower degree of CD4+ Tmem-cell functionality regarding IL-2, TNF-α and IFN-γ expression (Figure 2D—figure supplement 2A and B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the data shown in Figure 2D and figure supplement 2A and B.

claim: The frequencies of TNF-α+ Tmem cells within the IFN-γ+ PD-1+ CD4+ subpopulations were reduced with lupus nephritis.
source: The frequencies of TNF-α+ Tmem cells within the IFN-γ+ PD-1+ CD4+ subpopulations were reduced with lupus nephritis (Figure 2E), similar to CD8+ Tmem cells in chronic infections (Utzschneider et al., 2016).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the data in Figure 2E and compared to literature on chronic infections.

claim: Bins in the IFN-γhiPD-1–/low area contain the highest frequencies and expression levels of TNF-α and IL-2, but almost no IL-10 production.
source: Apparently, bins in the IFN-γhiPD-1–/low area contain the highest frequencies and expression levels of TNF-α and IL-2, but almost no IL-10 production (Figure 2F—figure supplement 2C and D).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the bin plot analysis shown in Figure 2F and figure supplement 2C and D.

claim: The low co-expression of IL-10 and IL-2 as well as TNF-α was confirmed by contour plots.
source: The low co-expression of IL-10 and IL-2 as well as TNF-α was confirmed by contour plots (Figure 2—figure supplement 3A).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the contour plots shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3A.

claim: A similar bin plot pattern of IL-10 (higher frequencies associated with a PD-1hi IFN-γlow phenotype) was discovered in all studied mice despite high differences in the frequencies of IL-10 expression per mouse and disease score.
source: We discovered a similar bin plot pattern of IL-10 (higher frequencies associated with a PD-1hi IFN-γlow phenotype) in all studied mice despite high differences in the frequencies of IL-10 expression per mouse and disease score (Figure 2—figure supplement 3B and D), and even when mice from a different experiment were concatenated (three mice each) (Figure 2—figure supplement 3C).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the reproducibility analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3B, C, and D.

claim: Varying the cut-off value for IL-10+ cells had a high impact on IL-10 frequencies, but almost no influence on their bin pattern.
source: Using IL-10 bin plots, we also demonstrated some general advantages of the PRI approach: (i) Varying the cut-off value for IL-10+ cells had a high impact on IL-10 frequencies, but almost no influence on their bin pattern (Figure 2—figure supplement 3E).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3E.

claim: The plotted bin area with 10 cells per bin provides statistically reliable data, as demonstrated by the relative standard error of the mean (RSEM).
source: (ii) The plotted bin area with 10 cells per bin provides statistically reliable data, as demonstrated by the relative standard error of the mean (RSEM) (Figure 2—figure supplement 3F).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the RSEM analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3F.

claim: IL-10 was found to be highly co-expressed with IL-21 (60%) in Tmem cells in SLE patients.
source: Recently, IL-10 was found to be highly co-expressed with IL-21 (60%) in Tmem cells in SLE patients (Facciotti et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: In NZBxW mice, there is neither substantial IL-10 and IL-21 co-expression with conventional contour plots nor strongly overlapping bin regions in bin plots on the TNF-α and IFN-γ plane.
source: Contrary to Facciotti et al., 2016, however, in NZBxW mice we observed neither substantial IL-10 and IL-21 co-expression with conventional contour plots nor strongly overlapping bin regions in bin plots on the TNF-α and IFN-γ plane (Figure 3A and D).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the data shown in Figure 3A and D, contrasting with previous findings in human SLE.

claim: IL-21 is particularly co-expressed with IL-2 and TNF-αhi in NZBxW mice.
source: In contrast, IL-21 is particularly co-expressed with IL-2 and TNF-αhi as demonstrated with contour plots and bin plots analyzing two (Figure 3A), three (Figure 3D) or four cytokines (Figure 3E) simultaneously.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the data shown in Figures 3A, 3D, and 3E.

claim: The PD-1low IL-21+ IFN-γ+ population was significantly higher in old compared to young mice.
source: However, they were not statistically significant in contrast to PD1hi cells of Tmem and CD44+ cells of CD4+ subset (Figure 3C). Gating for PD-1hi and PD-1low populations revealed that all populations studied had higher frequencies in older mice, but only the PD-1low IL-21+ IFN-γ+ population was significantly higher (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the statistical analysis shown in Figure 3C.

claim: In the NZBxW model, the expression of IL-21 is not correlated with a PD-1hi CXCR5+ Tfh cell phenotype.
source: Although IL-21 is a hallmark of Tfh cells, in the NZBxW model, the expression of IL-21 is not correlated with a PD-1hi CXCR5+ Tfh cell phenotype (Figure 3G—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the data shown in Figure 3G and figure supplement 1D.

claim: The frequencies of IL-21+ cells among Tmem cells do not change significantly with higher disease scores, but rather the properties of these cells to co-produce IFN-γ and PD-1.
source: Obviously, the frequencies of IL-21+ cells among Tmem cells do not change significantly with higher disease scores, but rather the properties of these cells to co-produce IFN-γ and PD-1 (Figure 3C and F—figure supplement 1B and C).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the data shown in Figure 3C, F, and figure supplement 1B and C.

claim: The identified PD-1low IL-21+ IFN-γhi cell subpopulation expressed high amounts of IL-2 and TNF-α in both young and old diseased mice.
source: The identified PD-1low IL-21+ IFN-γhi cell subpopulation even expressed high amounts of IL-2 and TNF-α in both young and old diseased mice.
evidence: This is based on the flow cytometry data presented in the manuscript.

claim: PD-1low IFN-γhi bins showed the highest probability of IL-21+ cells.
source: Again, PD-1low IFN-γhi bins showed the highest probability of IL-21+ cells.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the bin plot analysis shown in Figure 4.

claim: T cells in PD-1low IFN-γhi bins predominantly co-expressed CXCR3 and T-bet and lacked FoxP3 expression.
source: T cells in these bins predominantly co-expressed CXCR3 and T-bet and lacked FoxP3 expression.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the bin plot analysis shown in Figure 4A.

claim: The IL-21+ expression pattern overlapped only partially with that of Bcl6, CXCR5 or CXCR4.
source: The IL-21+ expression pattern overlapped only partially with that of Bcl6, CXCR5 or CXCR4 (Figure 4A—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the bin plot analysis shown in Figure 4A and figure supplement 1A.

claim: The IL-21+ IFN-γhi PD-1low Tmem cells additionally produced CD40L and ICOS, two receptors involved in the interaction of T and B cells.
source: Furthermore, the IL-21+ IFN-γhi PD-1low Tmem cells additionally produced CD40L and ICOS, two receptors involved in the interaction of T and B cells.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the bin plot analysis shown in Figure 4.

claim: CD40L was produced in the highest amounts by IFN-γhi cells.
source: CD40L was even produced in the highest amounts by IFN-γhi cells (Figure 4B—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the expression level analysis shown in Figure 4B and figure supplement 1A.

claim: The stimulatory receptors ICOS, OX40, GITR and CD27 showed lower intensities of expression in the PD-1low IFN-γhi bin area but higher intensities in the Tfh (Bcl6hi) bin area.
source: In contrast, the stimulatory receptors ICOS, OX40, GITR and CD27 showed lower intensities of expression in the PD-1low IFN-γhi bin area but higher intensities in the Tfh (Bcl6hi) bin area.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the bin plot analysis shown in Figure 4 and figure supplement 1.

claim: The inhibitory receptors TIGIT, CTLA4 and BTLA were mainly produced by Tfh cells, chronically activated T cells and/or Treg cells.
source: The same is true for the inhibitory receptors TIGIT, CTLA4 and BTLA, which were mainly produced by Tfh cells, chronically activated T cells and/or Treg cells (Figure 4B—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the bin plot analysis shown in Figure 4B and figure supplement 1.

claim: The properties and intermediate-to-high PSGL-1 expression suggest a Tfh-like cell subpopulation with Th1 properties instead of extrafollicular Tfh cells.
source: All these properties and their intermediate-to-high PSGL-1 expression suggest a Tfh-like cell subpopulation with Th1 properties instead of extrafollicular Tfh cells (Choi et al., 2015; Odegard et al., 2008).
evidence: This is an inference based on the observed marker expression patterns and comparison to literature.

claim: IL-21+ IFN-γhi PD-1low Tmem cells lacked CXCR5 expression.
source: As the IL-21+ IFN-γhi PD-1low Tmem cells lacked CXCR5 expression as other Tfh-like cells, we addressed their contribution to IL-21+ cells (Figure 5A and B) in spleen and their tissue distribution (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the data shown in Figure 5A and B.

claim: IL-21+ IFN-γhi PD-1low Tmem cells were localized in spleen and non-lymphoid organs, liver and lungs at comparable frequencies.
source: We were able to localize them in spleen and non-lymphoid organs, liver and lungs at comparable frequencies (Figure 5C and D).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the tissue distribution data shown in Figure 5C and D.

claim: IL-21+ IFN-γhi PD-1low Tmem cells were detected in kidneys and peripheral blood.
source: We could also detect them in kidneys and peripheral blood (Figure 5C and D and data not shown).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the tissue distribution data shown in Figure 5C and D.

claim: IL-21+ cells co-produced high levels of IFN-γ in all organs studied, but almost no CXCR5.
source: Again, IL-21+ cells co-produced high levels of IFN-γ in all these organs, but almost no CXCR5 (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the tissue distribution data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: The Tsh cell subset in diseased NZBxW mice is two times bigger than the Tph and 10 times bigger than the Tfh cell subset.
source: Interestingly, the Tsh cell subset in diseased NZBxW mice is two times bigger than the Tph and 10 times bigger than the Tfh cell subset.
evidence: This is based on the quantification of different T cell subsets shown in Figure 5.

claim: The highest frequencies of IL-21+ T cells were in PD-1low T cells, which was demonstrated by their normalization to CD44+ T cells.
source: These include the highest frequencies of IL-21+ T cells in PD-1low T cells, which was demonstrated by their normalization to CD44+ T cells (Figure 6C) and their positive correlation with the IFN-γ expression level (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the statistical analysis shown in Figure 6B and C.

claim: IL-21+ T cells showed a positive correlation with the IFN-γ expression level.
source: These include the highest frequencies of IL-21+ T cells in PD-1low T cells, which was demonstrated by their normalization to CD44+ T cells (Figure 6C) and their positive correlation with the IFN-γ expression level (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the statistical analysis shown in Figure 6B.

claim: CXCR5+ Bcl6+ (Tfh cells) predominantly appeared in bins at the PD-1hi side.
source: CXCR5+ Bcl6+ (Tfh cells) predominantly appeared in bins at the PD-1hi side, while there were only few bins with IL-21+ Bcl6+, IL-21+ CXCR5+ and even IL-21+ ICOShi T cells.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the bin plot analysis shown in Figure 6E.

claim: There were only few bins with IL-21+ Bcl6+, IL-21+ CXCR5+ and even IL-21+ ICOShi T cells.
source: CXCR5+ Bcl6+ (Tfh cells) predominantly appeared in bins at the PD-1hi side, while there were only few bins with IL-21+ Bcl6+, IL-21+ CXCR5+ and even IL-21+ ICOShi T cells.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the bin plot analysis shown in Figure 6E.

claim: The co-production of IL-21 and CD40L is localized in bins with IFN-γhi T cells.
source: Instead, the co-production of IL-21 and CD40L is localized in bins with IFN-γhi T cells (Figure 6E).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the bin plot analysis shown in Figure 6E.

claim: IL-21 expression levels did not correlate with Bcl6 and negatively with CXCR5.
source: IL-21 expression levels did not correlate with Bcl6 and negatively with CXCR5 (Figure 6G).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the histogram analysis shown in Figure 6G.

claim: Most IL-21+ CXCR5- cells are not PD-1hi but PD-1lo.
source: Plotting only IL-21+ CXCR5- cells in PRI-bins with a PD1hi threshold visualized Tsh and Tph cell subsets together. Most of these cells are not PD-1hi but PD-1lo (Figure 6F).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the bin plot analysis shown in Figure 6F.

claim: The main difference between the specified IL-21+ IFN-γhi PD-1low Tmem cells and previously described Tfh-like cell subpopulations is the high PD-1 expression which has been described for all previously identified Tfh-like subsets.
source: Next, we asked for similarities and differences between already described Tfh-like cell subpopulations (Choi et al., 2015; Hutloff, 2018; Vu Van et al., 2016) and the specified IL-21+ IFN-γhi PD-1low Tmem cells identified here. The main difference is the high PD-1 expression which has been described for all previously identified Tfh-like subsets, including the human Tph cells (Bocharnikov et al., 2019; Christophersen et al., 2019; Ekman et al., 2019; Rao et al., 2017).
evidence: This is based on comparison to literature on previously described Tfh-like cells.

claim: The most important similarities between the here specified and already known Tfh-like cells are the absence of CXCR5 and expression of ICOS and CD40Lhi.
source: The most important similarities between the here specified and already known Tfh-like cells, besides IL-21 expression, are the absence of CXCR5 and expression of ICOS and CD40Lhi (Figure 4A and B—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is based on the marker expression data shown in Figure 4 and comparison to literature.

claim: CXCR3+ served as a surrogate marker for IFN-γ production in FACS live sorting and helped to enrich IL-21+ IFN-γhi Tmem cells by a factor of five compared to CD44+ T cells.
source: CXCR3+ served as a surrogate marker for IFN-γ production in FACS live sorting and helped to enrich IL-21+ IFN-γhi Tmem cells by a factor of five compared to CD44+ T cells (Figure 4A, Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the sorting strategy shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

claim: Polyclonal stimulation of CXCR3+ T cells induced a high IgG production by B cells.
source: Polyclonal stimulation of these CXCR3+ T cells induced a high IgG production by B cells (Figure 7B) which was reduced either by blocking IL-21 or CD40L signaling and was abrogated by blocking both pathways (Figure 7B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the co-culture experiment shown in Figure 7B.

claim: IgG production by B cells co-cultured with CXCR3+ T cells was reduced either by blocking IL-21 or CD40L signaling and was abrogated by blocking both pathways.
source: Polyclonal stimulation of these CXCR3+ T cells induced a high IgG production by B cells (Figure 7B) which was reduced either by blocking IL-21 or CD40L signaling and was abrogated by blocking both pathways (Figure 7B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the blocking antibody experiments shown in Figure 7B.

claim: The blockade of IFN-γ did not diminish total IgG production by B cells co-cultured with CXCR3+ T cells.
source: We could rule out B cell helping activity of high IFN-γ levels of these cells, as reported for IgG2a induction (Snapper and Paul, 1987), since the blockade of IFN-γ did not diminish total IgG production (Figure 7B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the blocking antibody experiments shown in Figure 7B.

claim: PD-1low CXCR3+ Tsh cells promoted larger expansion of B cells than any other conditions, even outnumbering the positive control (IL-21 and anti-CD40) and PD-1hi cells by a factor of two and three, respectively.
source: Strikingly, PD-1low CXCR3+ Tsh cells promoted larger expansion of B cells than any other conditions, even outnumbering the positive control (IL-21 and anti-CD40) and PD-1hi cells by a factor of two and three, respectively (Figure 7C—figure supplement 2D).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the co-culture experiment shown in Figure 7C and figure supplement 2D.

claim: PD-1hi cells were clearly superior in preserving more viable B cells than the other conditions.
source: However, PD-1hi cells were clearly superior in preserving more viable B cells than the other conditions (Figure 7C—figure supplement 2D).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the co-culture experiment shown in Figure 7C and figure supplement 2D.

claim: The proportion of CD138+ antibody-producing B cells was higher in the co-cultures with PD-1hi cells (20% against 2–6% in other cultures).
source: While the proportion of CD138+ antibody-producing B cells was higher in the co-cultures with PD-1hi cells (20% against 2–6% in other cultures), Tsh cells induced 33% of the B cells to express the activation markers GL7 and Fas, typically used to define germinal center (GC) B cells, against 1.5% of B cells with a GC-like phenotype in PD-1hi co-cultures (Figure 7C—figure supplement 2D).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the co-culture experiment shown in Figure 7C and figure supplement 2D.

claim: Tsh cells induced 33% of the B cells to express the activation markers GL7 and Fas, typically used to define germinal center (GC) B cells, against 1.5% of B cells with a GC-like phenotype in PD-1hi co-cultures.
source: While the proportion of CD138+ antibody-producing B cells was higher in the co-cultures with PD-1hi cells (20% against 2–6% in other cultures), Tsh cells induced 33% of the B cells to express the activation markers GL7 and Fas, typically used to define germinal center (GC) B cells, against 1.5% of B cells with a GC-like phenotype in PD-1hi co-cultures (Figure 7C—figure supplement 2D).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the co-culture experiment shown in Figure 7C and figure supplement 2D.

claim: Tsh cells have highly potent helper capacity and suggests complementary functions to that of PD-1hi and Tfh cells during B cell differentiation.
source: Nevertheless, given the superiority of Tsh cells to promote B cell expansion, this experiment indicates that Tsh cells have highly potent helper capacity and suggests complementary functions to that of PD-1hi and Tfh cells during B cell differentiation.
evidence: This is an inference based on the co-culture experiment results shown in Figure 7.

claim: The IL-21 producing super-functional Th cells (IL-21+ IFN-γhi PD-1low Tmem cells) represent a novel Tfh-like subpopulation that can provide B-cell help in lupus nephritis mice in an IL-21- and CD40L-dependent manner.
source: All this suggests that the IL-21 producing super-functional Th cells (IL-21+ IFN-γhi PD-1low Tmem cells) represent a novel Tfh-like subpopulation that can provide B-cell help in lupus nephritis mice in an IL-21- and CD40L-dependent manner.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on all the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: PRI enabled the identification and characterization of the super-functional IL-21+ IFN-γhi cell subset.
source: First, PRI enabled the identification and characterization of the super-functional IL-21+ IFN-γhi cell subset by its main functionalities
evidence: This is a summary statement about the utility of the PRI method developed in this study.

claim: PRI provides simple visualization of the combinatorial properties of three markers and heat map representation of different statistical attributes of the third marker by binning conventional two-parametric dot plots.
source: (i) simple visualization of the combinatorial properties of three markers and heat map representation of different statistical attributes of the third marker by binning conventional two-parametric dot plots (e.g. Figure 1E, Figure 6E)
evidence: This describes a key feature of the PRI method demonstrated throughout the manuscript.

claim: PRI provides semi-continuous, combinatorial display that allows straightforward perception of correlating patterns.
source: (ii) semi-continuous, combinatorial display that allows straightforward perception of correlating patterns (e.g. Figure 3D–E)
evidence: This describes a key feature of the PRI method demonstrated throughout the manuscript.

claim: PRI provides reproducible pseudo-multi-parametric display of different markers so that subpopulations can be intuitively observed and compared, even between samples of different staining panels.
source: (iii) reproducible pseudo-multi-parametric display of different markers so that subpopulations can be intuitively observed and compared, even between samples of different staining panels, which is not applicable with cluster algorithms (e.g. Figure 4A and B; Qiu et al., 2011; Shen et al., 2018)
evidence: This describes a key feature of the PRI method demonstrated throughout the manuscript and compared to other methods.

claim: PRI enables exploitation of auxiliary information in percentages by the combinatorial approach, which would otherwise only be accessible with further gating steps.
source: (iv) exploitation of auxiliary information in percentages is enabled by the combinatorial approach, which would otherwise only be accessible with further gating steps.
evidence: This describes a key feature of the PRI method demonstrated throughout the manuscript.

claim: With PRI many cells and a broad bin range together with the right marker combination are necessary to obtain meaningful information from the plots.
source: It should also be noted, however, that with PRI many cells and a broad bin range together with the right marker combination are necessary to obtain meaningful information from the plots.
evidence: This is a limitation of the PRI method noted by the authors.

claim: PRI paves the way for reproducible and automatable cytometric analyses, which are useful not only for basic research but also for clinical studies.
source: PRI paves the way for reproducible and automatable cytometric analyses, which are useful not only for basic research but also for clinical studies to identify disease mechanisms and progressions, to discover biomarkers, to analyze therapy responder/non-responder, and to monitor stable quality and effectiveness of manipulated cells.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about the potential applications of the PRI method.
